title: Commit reservation with SQLite
scenario: The original order requests 3 from item 1's 5 units. Replace the controlled repository with SQLite: stock must fall to 2 and the reservation record must appear together. The transaction must prevent either write from succeeding alone. These isolated in-memory tests verify atomicity and commit behavior; they do not test process-crash recovery or persistence across restarts.
instructions: Implement SqliteReservationRepository in src/infrastructure/sqlite_repository.rs. observe selects the item row and delegates validation to decode_inventory_row. commit owns one SQLx transaction: conditionally subtract quantity with `available >= quantity`, return UnavailableAtCommit only if a zero-row update is rolled back successfully, insert a reservation with RETURNING reservation_id, validate the ID, then commit. Until transaction rollback is confirmed, classify an in-transaction failure conservatively as CommitOutcomeUnknown; lesson 6 will refine statement-failure mapping. Do not release a receipt before commit.

hints.body: observe uses `fetch_optional`, then transposes row decoding. Commit needs one transaction for the guarded UPDATE and reservation INSERT.
The UPDATE predicate is commit authority: match item ID and require `available >= requested`. If no row changes, explicitly roll back before returning UnavailableAtCommit.
Insert with RETURNING inside the same transaction; construct the receipt from intent and generated ID. Treat failures after begin as unknown until rollback is confirmed.

completionExplanation: The successful transaction commits both results together: stock 2 and one reservation receipt. A stale order changes neither. This in-memory test does not establish survival across process restarts. Next, distinguish a statement failure with confirmed rollback from a COMMIT failure whose transaction outcome may be unknown.
